members.name: low_vol_momentum_v1
members.thesis: The low-volatility anomaly (Ang et al. 2006) — low-vol stocks deliver higher risk-adjusted returns than high-vol stocks — manifests intraday in Indian markets. NIFTY 50 stocks in the bottom tercile of 20-day realized vol that also show positive intraday momentum (price > VWAP, EMA alignment) outperf
entry_long: low_vol == True (stock in bottom vol tercile)
intraday_momentum == True (above VWAP, EMAs aligned up)
entry_short: high_vol == True (stock in top vol tercile)
intraday_momentum == True for short (below VWAP, EMAs aligned down)
members.exit_target: long leg outperforms short leg by 30bps (relative target)
members.exit_stop: long leg underperforms short leg by 25bps OR either leg hits 0.5% absolute loss
filters: India_VIX < 20; low-vol anomaly weakens in high-VIX environments (all stocks become high-vol)
both long and short stocks must have avg volume > ₹100cr/day
NIFTY not in extreme trend (> 2%); factor bets work in moderate markets
weaknesses: The low-vol anomaly is primarily a cross-sectional effect over weeks/months; compressing it to intraday may not capture the same economic forces (institutional preference, leverage aversion)
Two-leg execution with stocks from different sectors creates idiosyncratic risk that may dominate the low-vol factor return on any given day
In risk-off environments (sharp selloffs), low-vol stocks also sell off, and the short high-vol leg may actually outperform (short squeeze), creating large losses
members.prior_art: Ang et al. (2006) cross-section of vol and returns; Baker et al. (2011) betting against beta; Blitz & Van Vliet (2007) low-vol effect. Intraday adaptation is novel.

members.name: smart_beta_intraday_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 100 constituents, bottom tercile by 5-day avg intraday range
members.thesis: The low-volatility anomaly (low-vol stocks deliver higher risk-adjusted returns) is documented at monthly horizons but has an intraday analog: stocks in the bottom tercile of realized intraday volatility (measured by 5-day average of intraday high-low range / close) that break out of their compresse
entry_long: Stock is in bottom tercile of 5-day avg intraday range (low-vol name)
entry_short: Stock is in bottom tercile of 5-day avg intraday range
members.exit_target: 60 bps from entry (low-vol stocks move less, target accordingly)
members.exit_stop: 30 bps from entry (tight stop — false breakouts in low-vol names are quick)
filters: India VIX < 22; low-vol breakout strategy works best in calm markets
NIFTY 50 EMA(20) slope > 0 for longs; < 0 for shorts
Bid-ask spread < 4 bps (tighter for low-vol names)
weaknesses: Low-vol stocks have smaller absolute moves — 60 bps target is ambitious for names in the bottom tercile of intraday range; many targets may not be hit within time stop
False breakouts in low-vol names often have low volume, making the volume filter critical but also restrictive — may only get 1-2 signals per week
The low-volatility anomaly is documented at monthly frequencies; its persistence at 1-min granularity is unproven and may not hold
members.prior_art: Baker, Bradley & Wurgler (2011) 'Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage'; Blitz & van Vliet (2007) low-volatility anomaly; NIFTY Low Volatility 30 index methodology; Keltner Channel breakouts in retail TA

members.name: overnight_vol_carry_v1
members.thesis: The overnight return variance (close-to-open) is systematically different from intraday return variance (open-to-close) in Indian equities. On average, the ratio of overnight vol to intraday vol for NIFTY 50 stocks is ~0.6, meaning stocks move less overnight than during the session. However, after n
entry_long: IF session_type == 'mean_rev': gap_pct < -0.5 AND RSI_14 < 35 (fade the overnight over-reaction, buy dip)
IF session_type == 'momentum': close > EMA_9 AND EMA_9 > EMA_21 AND time > 09:30 (ride the pent-up energy up)
entry_short: IF session_type == 'mean_rev': gap_pct > 0.5 AND RSI_14 > 65 (fade gap up)
IF session_type == 'momentum': close < EMA_9 AND EMA_9 < EMA_21 AND time > 09:30
members.exit_target: mean_rev: prev_close (gap fill); momentum: 1.5 * ATR_14 from entry
members.exit_stop: mean_rev: gap extends 40% further; momentum: 0.7 * ATR_14 from entry
filters: India_VIX < 22 for mean_rev; no VIX filter for momentum
momentum type: NIFTY must be moving in trade direction; mean_rev: NIFTY gap in same direction as stock (sector-wide overreaction)
weaknesses: The overnight vol ratio threshold (1.5 for mean-rev, 0.3 for momentum) is calibrated on historical data; these thresholds may shift as market microstructure evolves
On ~50% of days, the overnight_ratio is between 0.3-1.5 ('neutral'), generating no signals — strategy is highly capital-inefficient as standalone
The momentum sub-strategy (low overnight vol = intraday breakout) has only ~52% win rate, bringing down the blended performance
members.prior_art: French & Roll (1986) stock return variances: trading vs non-trading hours. Lockwood & Linn (1990) on overnight vs intraday volatility. Cliff et al. (2008) on overnight returns.
